title: Write the shoot button logic
summary: Use an if / else so the flywheel runs only while the shoot button is held.

say.never: The shooter's brain is in `updateLogic`. Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `ShooterSubsystem`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.
say.bit: Press **Ctrl+P**, type `ShooterSubsystem` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name.

say.never: Click in the code, then hold **Ctrl** and tap **F** to open the search box. Type `write the shoot button logic` and press **Enter**. The editor scrolls to the right spot and highlights it.
say.bit: Press **Ctrl+F**, type `write the shoot button logic` and press Enter to jump to it.

waitFor.hint: find write the shoot button logic with Ctrl+F.

steps.title: If the button is held, else stop

say.never: An `if` runs its block only when the question in the parentheses is true. Here the question is `OI.getShootButton()`: *is the driver holding the button right now?* The `else` block runs the rest of the time. Because `updateLogic` runs every 20 thousandths of a second, the flywheel starts the moment the button goes down and stops the moment it comes up. Write both blocks under the comment.
say.bit: `if (OI.getShootButton())` runs while the button is held; `else` runs the rest of the time. Set the flywheel's duty cycle in each.

marks.label: true while the button is held

say.never: Press **Start**, wait for **Running**, choose **Teleop**, press **Enable**, then hold **U** (right bumper). In AdvantageScope graph `Subsystem/Shooter/FlywheelVelocity`. Let go of **U** and watch it coast back down.
say.bit: Start, enable Teleop, hold **U**, and graph `Subsystem/Shooter/FlywheelVelocity`.
